common_mistakes: Submitting the project as a simple tenant improvement and not calling out the change of occupancy and occupant load increase — that will get bounced in plan review
Forgetting accessibility and egress upgrades for the new assembly/recreation use
Assuming the building permit covers electrical, mechanical, and plumbing work inside the tenant space
Starting demolition before the permit is issued and posted

Submitting permit application without verifying current contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city registration will block your application silently. Verify your registration is current BEFORE submitting.

pro_tips: Portland BDS is slow on commercial plan review — build in at least 6-8 weeks and expect correction cycles
Have the occupant load calculation and egress plan ready before submittal; that is usually where commercial change-of-use reviews stall
Check your Portland contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are the #1 avoidable rejection reason.
If the tenant space needs new HVAC or restroom ventilation, get those drawings coordinated before first submittal so you do not create a second review cycle

response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: Commercial zoning and use approval may be a major issue for a warehouse-to-indoor recreation conversion. Verify the site is allowed for indoor pickleball/recreation use, parking, accessibility, and any conditional use or design review requirements. HOA restrictions are usually not the issue for commercial property, but zoning overlays, downtown design standards, and any historic district rules can delay or block the project.
